info.title: Osmium
info.description:
Orchestration for a fleet of Minecraft agents that build a large schematic together.

An **agent** is one Minecraft session on one server. A **host** is a machine running the
Osmium host software, which owns its agents and is the only component that ever performs
a Minecraft login — the backend holds no Minecraft credentials and has no code path that
touches one. Commands are relayed to the owning host and answer **503** when it has no
live connection; they are never queued.

Routes authorize against **permission nodes**, never against role names. Roles are named
bundles of nodes arranged as nested tiers: `viewer`, `orchestrator`, `administrator`.
The node required by each route is listed on its 403 response.

Two channels sit outside this document. Hosts dial in over a WebSocket at `/ws/host`
with an enrolment token rather than a JWT. Browsers receive live updates as server-sent
events from `/api/stream/**`, which is receive-only — every command travels over the
REST routes below, where it is node-gated and written to the audit log.

See FLEET_CONNECTIVITY.md in the repository for the wire protocol and the reasoning.

put.summary: Replace the role of an account.
put.description: Roles are nested seniority levels, so an account holds exactly one or none. An account cannot change its own role, so an administrator cannot demote themselves.

409.description: The account is the caller's own.

put.description: The whole set of settings, not a patch: a key left out has been cleared. The keys are the interface's own and are relayed to the host uninterpreted, which ignores any it does not recognise. `connect.rejoin` is the one exception and is acted on here, since putting an agent back into the game is a decision a host is never allowed to make. Saved whether or not the host is reachable — configuration is a preference rather than an action, and an unreachable host is sent it on its next connection.

400.description: More configuration than an agent can hold.

put.summary: Point the agent at a Minecraft server, or at none.
put.description: Null unassigns it, leaving it set up and idle. Offline only: this decides what the next connection targets, and changing it under a live session would describe a session that is not happening. Credentials are untouched either way.

409.description: The agent is online.

post.summary: Create an account with a chosen username and password.

400.description: Blank username, short password or unknown role.

409.description: Username already taken.

post.summary: Sign an account out of every session.
post.description: Revokes every refresh token and every access token already issued to it, leaving the account itself alone. For when somebody's laptop is gone and they are not around to do it themselves.

409.description: The job is finished, the segment is built, or the agent is offline, on another server, or already holding a segment.
The job is finished, or the agent is offline, on another server, or already on a job.

post.description: Returns the enrolment token once. Only its hash is stored, so it cannot be retrieved later - a lost token is replaced by re-enrolling. No address is taken: the host connects to Osmium, so its location is observed on connect.

409.description: Name already enrolled.

post.description: Invalidates the previous token and closes the host's current connection, so it must reconnect with the new one. Use this instead of deleting a host when a token leaks - the host keeps its agents.

409.description: The plan is unplaced, its schematic is not read, the agents are not all online on one server, or this build is already running.

post.summary: Sign out of every session, everywhere.
post.description: Revokes every refresh token **and** every access token already issued — the latter is what a password change alone did not do.
Marks it read. A later replay raises it again.

post.summary: Mint a new access token from the refresh cookie.
post.description: Rotates: the presented token is spent and a successor replaces the cookie. The session expiry does not move, so refreshing cannot extend a session past its login.

200.description: A new access token, and a rotated cookie.

401.description: No cookie, or a token that is unknown, expired, revoked or replayed. A replay revokes every session descended from that login.

post.summary: Rotate the password of the authenticated account.
post.description: Requires the current password. Any authenticated account may call this for itself.

401.description: Missing token or wrong current password.

post.description: Revokes the refresh token and every successor of it, then clears the cookie.
The access token comes back in the body, for the caller to hold in memory. The refresh token is set as an HttpOnly cookie and never reaches JavaScript.
Nothing has touched Minecraft at this point; the agent starts UNLINKED.

409.description: Label already in use.

post.summary: Mint a one-shot ticket for this agent's viewer socket.
post.description:
Open `/ws/viewer` with `new WebSocket(url, ['osmium-viewer', ticket])`. The ticket is single-use, expires in 30 seconds, and is good for this agent only. It goes in the subprotocol rather than the query string so that it stays out of access logs and browser history.

The socket carries binary frames only, and is receive-only: acting on an agent goes over REST, where it is node checked and audited.

post.summary: Ask the host to set this agent up.
post.description: Sends `setup_agent` and moves the agent to SETUP_PENDING. Osmium does not perform or observe the login - the host reports back a verdict.

409.description: Setup already running, or the agent is online.

503.description: The owning host is not connected.

delete.summary: Stop waiting on a setup that was never completed.
delete.description: Returns the agent to UNLINKED so it can be set up again. **Nothing is sent to the host** — Osmium cannot cancel a login it does not perform, only stop asserting one is in progress. A host that finishes it afterwards still reports, and the agent still links.

409.description: No setup is in progress.

post.summary: Disconnect the agent from its Minecraft server.

409.description: The agent is not online.

503.description: The owning host is not connected.

post.summary: Connect the agent to its Minecraft server.
post.description: Sends `connect` and moves the agent to CONNECTING. The outcome arrives on the host's own schedule as ONLINE or CONNECT_FAILED; a host that reports neither is given a fixed window, after which the agent falls back to LINKED.

409.description: Already connecting, not set up, or assigned to no server.

503.description: The owning host is not connected.

post.summary: Speak in game as this agent.
post.description: Impersonation: this says something under an account you own, so it is gated separately from every other verb. Rate limited per agent, because chat spam is the fastest route to a Minecraft ban and the ban lands on the account, not the operator.

409.description: The agent is not online.

429.description: This agent has been made to speak too often.

503.description: The owning host is not connected.

delete.description: An account cannot delete itself, so an administrator cannot lock themselves out.

409.description: The account is the caller's own.

patch.description: Supplying a password resets it without knowing the current one. An account cannot target itself here - use PATCH /api/users/me and POST /api/auth/password - so changing your own password always requires the current one.

400.description: Blank username or password outside the allowed length.

409.description: Username already taken, or the account is the caller's own.

patch.description: Renaming yourself invalidates tokens issued under the old username, since the token subject no longer resolves. Log in again afterwards.

409.description: Username already taken.

delete.description: Cascades to its agents, which cannot run without it. Invalidates the token.

patch.description: Only the name is editable; address, version and reachability are observed from the connection rather than configured.

409.description: Name already enrolled.

patch.description: Omitted fields are left alone. Where an agent plays is set through `PUT /api/agents/{id}/server`, which has its own preconditions.

409.description: Label already taken.

get.summary: Stream everything this account is entitled to see change.
get.description:
Events: `agent`, `agent-removed`, `host`, `host-removed`, `chat`, `activity`, `telemetry`, `user`, `user-removed`, `audit`, `permissions`. Resource payloads match the REST responses, so a client replaces what it holds rather than refetching; `chat`, `activity` and `audit` are single lines to append, and `telemetry` is `{ agentId, telemetry }` to merge, published on a fixed tick rather than per reported sample.

**Each event carries its own permission.** Opening the stream needs only `user.read.self`, since every account has to be able to hear about itself; what actually arrives is decided per event, so `agent` reaches only `agent.read` and `audit` only `audit.read`. `permissions` is addressed to a single account when its own role changes and carries what `/api/auth/me` returns. Authority is re-read on a 30s tick, so a demotion narrows an open stream rather than needing a reconnect.

The same events as the whole stream, filtered to this agent. A server's global chat arrives here too, under whichever agent currently forwards it, so a view showing one agent's conversation filters on `scope`.

get.summary: List every role with its permission nodes.
The tiles inside a rectangle of chunks.
get.description:
Coordinates are **chunks, not blocks** - divide a block coordinate by 16, rounding down.
            Both corners are included.

            `dimension` is required and is not a filter but part of the address: the worlds are
            separate places that share a coordinate system, so `0,0` in the Nether and `0,0` in the
            Overworld are different ground. Ask `/api/map/servers` for the ones that exist.

            Bounded rather than paged, because a map is drawn as an area rather than read as a list.
            At most 4096 chunks in one request, which is a kilometre square - past that, ask for a
            smaller window and draw at a coarser zoom.

            Tiles carry block *names*. What colour a block is, is a question about textures, and
            Osmium stores none: the caller holds the palette. Missing chunks are simply absent -
            nowhere in the response says a chunk has never been charted, because it is the same
            answer as one nobody has walked over yet.

parameters.name: server
parameters.description: The server whose map to read.

200.description: Every charted chunk in the area.

400.description: An inside-out area, or one larger than 4096 chunks.

get.summary: Which servers and worlds have a map, and how much of one.
get.description:
One row per server **and dimension**, newest activity first: they are separate maps at
            the same coordinates, so a server that has been walked in the Overworld and the Nether
            appears twice.

            The extent is in chunk coordinates and is what a screen needs to decide where to point
            itself before it asks for any tiles.

200.description: Every server with at least one charted chunk.

409.description: The job is still building; pause it first.

200.description: The blocks, in the packed segment format.

401.description: No ticket, or one that names nothing.

409.description: The job is finished, or the segment is no longer being built.

get.summary: One page of chat, newest first.
get.description:
Pass exactly one of `agentId` or `server`.

            `agentId` gives the conversation to or about that agent, and excludes the global
            channel: that is identical for every agent on the server and would bury the lines that
            are actually about the one you are looking at.

            `server` gives everything that happened there - the global channel forwarded once by the
            elected listener, plus whispers, proximity chat and the agents' own outbound lines. Not
            the mirror of the above: a whisper to one agent is still something that happened on that
            server.

            `query` searches the message text and the sender, case-insensitively, and narrows
            whichever of the two filters was given. With neither, it searches every server the fleet
            was listening to - a phrase somebody half-remembers rarely comes with the server it was
            said on.

            Pages by cursor, not by offset: chat arrives while it is being read. Send `nextCursor`
            from the previous response to continue. Kept for 3 days.

parameters.name: agentId
parameters.description: Conversation to or about this agent. Excludes the server's global chat.

parameters.name: server
parameters.description: Global chat on this server address.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Search the text and the sender, case-insensitively. With neither `agentId` nor `server`, searches every server the fleet was listening to.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many lines to return. Clamped to 1..500.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `nextCursor` from the previous page. Omit for the newest lines.

400.description: Both filters given, neither given without a `query`, or a malformed `cursor`.

get.description: Accepts a Minecraft username or UUID. Fetched from a skin service and cached, so no operator's browser talks to it directly.

404.description: No head: unknown player, malformed identifier, upstream unavailable, or avatars disabled. The caller renders its own fallback either way.

get.description: Only the tip of each rotation chain, with the caller's own marked. The address is only meaningful where the deployment's proxy headers are trusted, and the user agent is self-declared by the browser.

get.summary: One page of operator actions, newest first.
get.description:
Pages by cursor, not by offset: the trail grows while it is being read, so an offset
            would repeat or skip entries between requests. Send `nextCursor` from the previous
            response to continue; a null `nextCursor` means the trail ended.

            Entries are kept for 30 days by default and purged daily.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many entries to return. Clamped to 1..500.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `nextCursor` from the previous page. Omit for the newest entries.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Narrows to entries whose account, target, detail or action matches.

200.description: A page of entries, oldest continuing at `nextCursor`.

get.summary: The trail for a date range, as a CSV attachment.
get.description:
`from` is inclusive and `to` exclusive, both ISO-8601 instants, so the caller decides
            what timezone a "day" means rather than having UTC assumed for it.

            The range is capped at the moment the export starts, so a `to` in the future is not an
            error and the file cannot contain the record of its own export.

            Columns are `at,account,action,target,detail`, always in English and never translated:
            an export is read by tooling and kept as a record, so its shape cannot depend on who
            pressed the button. Every field is quoted, and a value a spreadsheet would run as a
            formula keeps its text and gains a leading apostrophe.

            Writes an audit entry of its own before any row is sent.

get.summary: One page of agent incidents, newest first.
get.description:
Every agent's incidents merged, or one agent's when `agentId` is given.

            Pages by cursor, not by offset: incidents arrive while the feed is being read. Send
            `nextCursor` from the previous response to continue. Kept for 10 days.

parameters.name: agentId
parameters.description: Narrow to one agent. Omit for the whole fleet.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many entries to return. Clamped to 1..500.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `nextCursor` from the previous page. Omit for the newest entries.

delete.summary: End one of your own sessions.
delete.description: Ending the current one leaves this browser signed out at the next refresh.

404.description: No such session **for this account**. Another operator's session is reported the same way as one that does not exist.

UpdateRoleRequest.description: Replaces the role of an account. Null clears it, leaving no permissions.

UserResponse.description: A user account. Passwords are never returned.

role.description: Assigned role, or null when the account has none.

nodes.description: Permission nodes granted by the assigned role.

sessionAlertAt.description: When a refresh token for this account was replayed, if the operator has not been shown it yet. Null the rest of the time, which is nearly always.

AgentSettingsRequest.description: What an operator has configured for an agent. The keys are the interface's own and are relayed to the host uninterpreted; a host ignores any it does not recognise.

values.description: Every setting, not a patch. A key left out has been cleared.

AgentResponse.description: An agent. Only its Minecraft identity is stored, never a credential.

serverAddress.description: Where it plays, or null when it is assigned nowhere and cannot connect.

state.description: Stored state, adjusted to STALE when the owning host is unreachable.

onlineSince.description: When the agent last entered the game. Null while it is not online.

telemetry.description: Latest vitals, or null when the agent has not reported recently.

chatListener.description: True when this agent forwards its server's global chat. One per server, elected by the backend - a server with none has no global feed.

rejoining.description: True while Osmium still intends to put this agent back in the game: it was connected on purpose and is not online. Covers the wait between attempts as well as an attempt in flight, so an interface can offer to stop trying. Cleared by a disconnect.

AgentTelemetryResponse.description: An agent's latest reported vitals. Never stored - if an agent has not reported recently this is null, rather than showing something an hour old as though it were now.

pingMs.description: Round trip to the Minecraft server.

NearbyPlayerResponse.description: A player standing near an agent in game.

position.description: Where the player is, when the host reported it.

uuid.description: Their account, for drawing the right head. Null when unreported.

ping.description: Round trip as the server measures it, in ms.

AssignServerRequest.description: Points an agent at a Minecraft server, or at none. Separate from both setup and editing: the account is the same account wherever it joins, so where it plays is its own decision and changing it touches no credential.

serverAddress.description: Null unassigns it, leaving the agent set up and idle.

CreateUserRequest.description: Creates an account with an administrator-chosen username and password.

role.description: Role name to assign. Must already exist. Omit for no permissions.

AssignSegmentRequest.description: Hands one segment to one agent.

BuildJobResponse.description: One execution of one build, on one server.

state.description: ACTIVE, DONE or CANCELLED. There is no failed job.

requestedParts.description: How many pieces were asked for. `segments` can be fewer.

placement.description: The anchor as it stood when the job started.

blocksPlaced.description: The sum of the segments' last reported counts.

pool.description: Who is working this job. Empty once it is finished.

finishedAt.description: Null while the job is active.

JobAgentResponse.description: One agent working a job, whether or not it is holding a piece right now.

agentId.description: Null once the agent has been deleted.

JobSegmentResponse.description: One agent's share of a job, in world coordinates. `max` is exclusive.

state.description: PENDING, ASSIGNED, BUILDING, DONE or FAILED.

agentId.description: Null when nobody holds it, or when the agent has since been removed.

agentLabel.description: Kept after the agent is gone, so the record still says who built it.

blocksPlaced.description: Last reported, never accumulated. Survives a release.

lastReportAt.description: Null until a host has reported on this segment.

failureReason.description: Why the host could not build it. Null unless FAILED.

blockedBy.description: Unfinished pieces beneath this one. Empty means it is ready.

releasedFrom.description: Agent this was released from, and will not be given back to.

JobSubstitutionResponse.description: One block swapped for another, as it stood when the job started.

PlacementRequest.description: Where the schematic's minimum corner lands in the world.

AddJobAgentRequest.description: Puts one agent on a job. Which piece it gets is the scheduler's business.

CreateHostRequest.description: Enrols a host. No address: the host dials in, so its location is observed.

HostEnrolledResponse.description: A freshly enrolled host, with its enrolment token shown exactly once.

token.description: Give this to the host. It is hashed on the server and never shown again.

HostResponse.description: A host. Reachability is derived from the heartbeat, not stored.

hostVersion.description: Observed when the host connects. Null until it first dials in.

loginMethods.description: What this host can log in with, from its handshake. Empty while it is disconnected, and empty for a host that advertises nothing - which can then set nothing up.

LoginMethodResponse.description: A login mechanism the host advertised in its handshake. The id is opaque to the backend and is relayed to the host verbatim; the copy describes a mechanism, never an account.

CreateBuildRequest.description: Creates a build. Placement and substitutions can both be settled later.

SubstitutionRequest.description: One block swapped for another. A null or blank replacement means place nothing at all, which is the honest answer to not having the material.

BuildResponse.description: A build: a schematic, where it goes, and what it is built out of.

placement.description: Null until the build has been placed.

placed.description: False while it has nowhere to stand, whatever else is settled.

StartJobRequest.description: Starts building a plan with a pool of agents. One job, one server.

mode.description: How to divide the build. COLUMNS is the safe default.

parts.description: Pieces to divide into. Defaults to the size of the pool.

token.description: Signed JWT to send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

PasswordChangeRequest.description: Rotates the password of the authenticated account.

CreateAgentRequest.description: Creates an agent slot. Nothing has touched Minecraft at this point.

serverAddress.description: Where it should play, if that is already known.

SetupAgentRequest.description: Asks the host to set the agent up. The method is a mechanism the operator chose, relayed to the host uninterpreted. It must never identify an account.

method.description: One of the ids the owning host advertised in its handshake. Anything else is refused, and a host that advertised nothing can set nothing up.

ChatRequest.description: Sends a chat message as an agent. This is impersonation - gated on chat.

UpdateUserRequest.description: Edits any account. Only an administrator can set a password without knowing the old one.

password.description: Omit to leave the password untouched.

UpdateSelfRequest.description: Edits the authenticated account. The role is deliberately not editable here.

UpdateHostRequest.description: Renames a host. Everything else about a host is observed, not configured.

UpdateBuildRequest.description: Edits a build. Omitted fields are left as they are.

UpdateAgentRequest.description: Renames an agent. Where it plays is set through `PUT /api/agents/{id}/server`, which is a different kind of change and has its own preconditions.

RoleResponse.description: A role and the permission nodes it grants.

MapAreaResponse.description: The tiles inside the requested area.

MapTileResponse.description: One chunk of the world seen from above: 16x16 pixels, one per block column, at the resolution of an in-game map at full zoom.

MapExtentResponse.description: What one world of one server's map covers, in chunk coordinates.

ChatMessageResponse.description: One line of Minecraft chat, as the agent that observed it reported it.

ChatPageResponse.description: One page of chat, newest first.

SessionResponse.description: One live session. Only the tip of each rotation chain is listed — a spent token is a step in a chain, not something an operator would recognise.

startedAt.description: When this link in the chain was issued.

expiresAt.description: When the session ends regardless of use. Refreshing does not move it.

clientIp.description: Where it was last seen from, or null when the request carried nothing usable. Only meaningful where the deployment's proxy headers are trusted.

userAgent.description: Self-declared by the browser, and not evidence of anything.

current.description: True for the session making this request - the one not to end by accident.

AuditEntryResponse.description: One operator action: who did what, to which agent or host.

AuditPageResponse.description: One page of the trail, newest first.

ActivityEntryResponse.description: Something that happened to an agent: kicked, died, connected, relink needed.

ActivityPageResponse.description: One page of activity, newest first.

bearerAuth.description: Obtain one from POST /api/auth/login. Send as `Bearer <token>`.
